[Pedagogy review · High priority · opening-review · pf-07c18673e1]
At p4-calculating-heights-static-model: Before the solid examples, add: '(a) A right triangle has perpendicular sides 6 cm and 8 cm. Write an equation and find its hypotenuse x. (b) A right triangle has hypotenuse 13 mm and one shorter side 5 mm. Write an equation and find the other side y. (c) A right triangle has hypotenuse 7 m and one shorter side 3 m. Find the other side z in exact surd form.' Answers: x² = 6² + 8², x = 10 cm; y² + 5² = 13², y = 12 mm; z = √40 m. Keep the review within one page.
Also affects: p4-example-heights

[Pedagogy review · High priority · opening-review · pf-aa0adbcdce]
Before p6-information-text, add: '(a) Find the area of a rectangle 8 cm by 5 cm. (b) Find the area of a triangle with base 8 cm and perpendicular height 6 cm. (c) Find the combined area of two triangles, each with base 5 cm and perpendicular height 7 cm.' Answers: 40 cm², 24 cm², 35 cm². Keep the review within one page.

[Pedagogy review · Suggestion · extension · pf-9eb6a938a9]
Append parts to p7-q1-a: (i) A second pyramid has the same 12 cm square base, but each triangular face has perpendicular height 24 cm. Find its total surface area. Answer: 720 cm². (ii) Explain why this is less than twice the original total surface area. Answer: The triangular areas double, but the 144 cm² base area stays unchanged.

[Pedagogy review · High priority · opening-review · pf-9c33f21049]
At p13-information-block: Before the cone definition, add: '(a) Write the formula for the area of a circle. (b) A circle has diameter 18 cm. Find its radius. (c) Find the area of a circle with diameter 10 cm, leaving your answer in terms of π.' Answers: πr²; 9 cm; 25π cm².
Also affects: p13-examples

[Pedagogy review · Suggestion · variation-sequence · pf-1509d22427]

(e) r = 3 cm, l = 6 cm. (f) r = 3 cm, l = 8 cm. (g) Diameter 8 cm, l = 7 cm.' Answers: 65.97 cm², 84.82 cm², 103.67 cm², 138.23 cm². Keep the orientation fixed through d–f.

[Pedagogy review · Suggestion · extension · pf-c5e0f8cdf4]
Append parts to p23-q9: (a) If the cylinder diameter becomes 2 cm and its height remains 3 cm, find the total surface area to 1 d.p. Answer: 103.7 cm². (b) If its diameter becomes 6 cm and its height remains 3 cm, find the total surface area to 1 d.p. Answer: 141.4 cm². (c) Explain why the cylinder top and exposed flat part of the hemisphere have combined area 9π cm² in all three versions. Answer: The cylinder top replaces an equal area covered at the join.

[Pedagogy review · Suggestion · extension · pf-9b6919c521]
After p5-q2-b, add: '(i) Find the perpendicular height of this pyramid in exact surd form. (ii) List the perpendicular height, face slant height and side edge from shortest to longest.' Answers: (i) √4633 mm; (ii) √4633 mm < 77 mm < 85 mm.

[Pedagogy review · Suggestion · extension · pf-20d6b57e30]
After p12-q8, add: '(b) A second right square pyramid has the same base area and perpendicular height 56 m. Find its surface area to the nearest square metre. (c) Is its triangular-face area twice that of the original pyramid? Explain why using the two slant heights.' Answers: (b) 6788 m²; (c) No. The slant heights are 35 m and √3577 m ≈ 59.8 m, so the triangular-face area is multiplied by about 1.71.

[Pedagogy review · Suggestion · extension · pf-aa0938687d]
After p20-q1-c, add parts: '(d) Find the surface area of a sphere with radius 12 m, correct to two decimal places. (e) How many spheres with radius 6 m have the same combined surface area as one sphere with radius 12 m?' Answers: (d) 1809.56 m²; (e) 4.
